entries.summary: DeepSeek Search and DeepSeek Fetch are now available through AI Gateway. Search finds relevant pages with titles, URLs, and summaries. Fetch retrieves page content as Markdown for your model to read.Use both tools with any model that supports tool calling, using one AI Gateway API key. entries.content:
DeepSeek Search and DeepSeek Fetch are now available through AI Gateway. Search finds relevant pages with titles, URLs, and summaries. Fetch retrieves page content as Markdown for your model to read.

Use both tools with any model that supports tool calling, using one AI Gateway API key. No separate DeepSeek account is required, and you can keep the same tools when switching model providers.

These helpers are available in AI SDK 6.0.321 and later on v6, or 7.0.160 and later on v7. Update with 

pnpm add ai@latest
and set your 
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
. To combine search and page retrieval, pass both helpers in 
tools
: 
      
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';const result = streamText({  model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017',  prompt: 'Find the latest Vercel AI Gateway announcement, fetch it, and summarize it.',  tools: {    deepseek_search: gateway.tools.deepseekSearch({ count: 3 }),    deepseek_fetch: gateway.tools.deepseekFetch(),  },});for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

You can also use alternative search tools with DeepSeek Fetch if DeepSeek Search fails:

      
import { gateway, streamText } from 'ai';const result = streamText({  model: 'zai/glm-5.3-flash',  system: 'Try deepseek_search, then exa_search, then parallel_search on errors. After search succeeds, use deepseek_fetch on a result URL.',  prompt: 'Find the latest Vercel AI Gateway announcement, fetch it, and summarize it.',  toolChoice: 'required',  tools: {    deepseek_search: gateway.tools.deepseekSearch({ count: 3 }),    deepseek_fetch: gateway.tools.deepseekFetch(),    exa_search: gateway.tools.exaSearch({ numResults: 3 }),    parallel_search: gateway.tools.parallelSearch({ maxResults: 3 }),  },});for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

Search fallback is model-directed, so provider order and retry limits are best effort. DeepSeek Fetch can retrieve a result URL from any of these search tools.

Search and Fetch each cost $0.75 per 1,000 billable requests. Failed requests, timeouts, and empty results have no tool charge. Model tokens are billed separately.

See the DeepSeek Search documentation and DeepSeek Fetch documentation for configuration options and pricing details.

AI Gateway provides one API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring routing, retries, and failover. You can use an AI Gateway API key or bring your own provider key.

entries.summary: You can now set a new project to expire when you deploy it with Vercel CLI. Expired projects are deleted automatically, so prototypes, demos, and test apps don't need cleaning up by hand.Run vercel deploy with --delete-project-after and a duration:Supported durations are 1h, 1d, 1w, 2w, and 30d, and the CLI prints the date and time when the project expires. entries.content:
You can now set a new project to expire when you deploy it with Vercel CLI. Expired projects are deleted automatically, so prototypes, demos, and test apps don't need cleaning up by hand.

Run 

vercel deploy
with 
--delete-project-after
and a duration: 
      
# Delete the new project after one dayvercel deploy --delete-project-after 1d

Deploying a new project that expires after one day

Supported durations are 

1h
, 
1d
, 
1w
, 
2w
, and 
30d
, and the CLI prints the date and time when the project expires. The flag only applies when 
vercel deploy
creates the project. If you deploy to an existing project with the flag, its expiration doesn't change and the CLI prints a warning.

To remove a project's expiration, run 

vercel project keep
:

      
vercel project keep my-project

Removing a project's expiration

Update Vercel CLI to 

v65.12.0
or later to get started. Learn more in the vercel deploy documentation.

entries.title: Vercel Tracing is now generally available
entries.summary: Vercel Tracing is now generally available on all plans. You can now search and inspect traces from the dashboard or the Vercel CLI, and new Next.js projects get tracing by default. Pricing is unchanged from the beta.Browse and search traces in the dashboardIn beta, you could only open a trace per request from the Logs page. The new Traces page shows every trace and span in one place, for a project
entries.content:
Vercel Tracing is now generally available on all plans. You can now search and inspect traces from the dashboard or the Vercel CLI, and new Next.js projects get tracing by default. Pricing is unchanged from the beta.

Copy link to headingBrowse and search traces in the dashboard

In beta, you could only open a trace per request from the Logs page. The new Traces page shows every trace and span in one place, for a project or your whole team. Switch between a Spans list and a Traces list, filter each, and search with Kibana Query Language (KQL). A Live mode streams new traces as they arrive. A query like 

span.name:db* AND span.duration > 500
narrows to slow database spans by name and duration.

Copy link to headingSearch traces from the CLI

The Traces page uses the same KQL as 

vercel traces search --query
, so a query built in the dashboard runs in the CLI unchanged. Search covers every project in your team, or one project with the 
--project
flag. Inspect a single trace with 
vercel traces inspect
, and manage a project's sampling rules with 
vercel traces config
. 
      
vercel traces search --query 'span.duration > 2000'vercel traces search --status error --since 1h

Find spans slower than two seconds, then every error from the last hour.

Copy link to headingAutomatic tracing for new Next.js projects

In beta, nothing was collected until you added a sampling rule. Starting with Next.js 16.5, new projects created on Vercel that include at least one Node.js function get tracing turned on after their first successful build. Vercel adds one sampling rule tracing 100% of requests in all environments and injects instrumentation at build time, so traces include Next.js framework spans with no setup. To opt out, remove all sampling rules in Settings → Tracing.

Copy link to headingLonger retention

In beta, traces followed your runtime log retention. Hobby now keeps traces for 3 days instead of 1 hour, Pro for 14 days instead of 1 day, and Enterprise for 14 days instead of 3 days.

Read the Tracing documentation to learn more.

entries.title: Token Pass credit now applies automatically across AI Gateway
entries.summary: Token Pass credit now applies automatically to included model usage through AI Gateway, whether a request authenticates with an API key, OIDC token, or fx login. No dedicated Token Pass API key is required, though you can still create one from the dashboard or the CLI for keys scoped only to featured models and providers.When Token Pass credit runs out for the billing period, requests from a stand
entries.content:
Token Pass credit now applies automatically to included model usage through AI Gateway, whether a request authenticates with an API key, OIDC token, or fx login. No dedicated Token Pass API key is required, though you can still create one from the dashboard or the CLI for keys scoped only to featured models and providers.

When Token Pass credit runs out for the billing period, requests from a standard key or OIDC token fall back to your team's AI Gateway credits. Token Pass keys still stop until the next billing period.

Requests served through the Token Pass provider remain Zero Data Retention (ZDR). Fallback requests follow your team's setting. With team-wide ZDR enabled, they route only to ZDR providers.

Available now for Token Pass subscribers on Pro teams. If you created a Token Pass key during setup, switch to a standard API key or OIDC token to get fallback. Learn more in the Token Pass documentation.

entries.title: Ampersand from Humans& now available on AI Gateway
entries.summary: Ampersand from Humans& is now available on AI Gateway for free through November 13, 2026.Ampersand is a language model built to take part in group conversations, such as a team chat, and to decide on each turn whether to speak or stay quiet. It is designed to understand individual and shared goals, help people work through disagreements, and recognize when a contribution would be useful. That can
entries.content:
Ampersand from Humans& is now available on AI Gateway for free through November 13, 2026.

Ampersand is a language model built to take part in group conversations, such as a team chat, and to decide on each turn whether to speak or stay quiet. It is designed to understand individual and shared goals, help people work through disagreements, and recognize when a contribution would be useful. That can mean asking a clarifying question, sharing relevant context, or waiting while people respond to one another.

Your application exposes these actions as caller-defined function tools. 

send_message
delivers a contribution, while 
pass
leaves the conversation quiet until the next human message. Your application executes both tools and records their results. Leave tool choice at its default, since Ampersand accepts 
auto
and 
none
but rejects 
required
and named tool choices.

Call it through the AI SDK, the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API, or a coding agent. Use 

humansand/ampersand-v0.1
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText, tool, stepCountIs, type ModelMessage } from 'ai';import { z } from 'zod';
const messages: ModelMessage[] = [];const deliveries = new Map();const tools = {  send_message: tool({    description: 'Send a message to the group conversation.',    inputSchema: z.object({ content: z.string().trim().min(1) }).strict(),  }),  pass: tool({    description: 'Stay quiet until another human message arrives.',    inputSchema: z.object({}).strict(),  }),};
async function deliverMessage(content: string, receipt: string) {  const existing = deliveries.get(receipt);  if (existing !== undefined) return existing;  const messageId = `message_${deliveries.size + 1}`;  console.log(`Ampersand: ${content}`);  deliveries.set(receipt, messageId);  return messageId;}
async function onHumanMessage(content: string) {  messages.push({ role: 'user', content });  const result = streamText({    model: 'humansand/ampersand-v0.1',    maxRetries: 0,    system: 'Use send_message to contribute or pass to stay quiet. Choose one action.',    messages,    tools,    toolChoice: 'auto',    stopWhen: stepCountIs(1),    providerOptions: {      openai: { reasoningEffort: 'high', store: false, parallelToolCalls: false },    },  });
  for await (const part of result.fullStream) {    if (part.type === 'error') throw part.error;  }  const calls = await result.toolCalls;  const call = calls[0];  if (    (await result.finishReason) !== 'tool-calls' ||    calls.length !== 1 ||    call === undefined ||    call.dynamic  ) {    throw new Error('Expected one completed send_message or pass action');  }
  // Save the complete assistant response before delivering the validated action.  const response = await result.response;  messages.push(...response.messages);  const receipt = `${response.id}:${call.toolCallId}`;  const output = call.toolName === 'send_message'    ? await deliverMessage(call.input.content, receipt)    : 'Passing.';  messages.push({    role: 'tool',    content: [{      type: 'tool-result',      toolCallId: call.toolCallId,      toolName: call.toolName,      output: { type: 'text', value: output },    }],  });}
await onHumanMessage(  'Maya: I prefer green. Leo: I prefer blue. Ask one clarifying question.',);await onHumanMessage(  'Maya: Thanks. Leo, answer first. Ampersand, stay quiet until Leo replies.',);

The first human message invites a contribution; the second asks Ampersand to wait. In a chat application, call the handler when a new human message arrives. Handling 

pass
records the waiting action without posting a message or starting another model turn. For a deployed chat application, persist the response, history, and delivery receipts in durable storage. Retry uncertain delivery with the saved action and the same receipt, process messages sequentially per conversation, and check conversation access before posting.

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

humansand/ampersand-v0.1
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try Ampersand in the model playground.

entries.title: Vercel Schedules is now in public beta
entries.summary: Vercel Schedules is now in public beta on all plans. Run tasks on a recurring cadence or at a single point in time, in production, preview, or custom environments.Schedules in vercel.json can target a private Vercel Function, an HTTP path, or a Vercel Queue topic, and schedules created at runtime target a Queue topic. Any schedule can be enabled, disabled, or run on demand without redeploying.Defi
entries.content:
Vercel Schedules is now in public beta on all plans. Run tasks on a recurring cadence or at a single point in time, in production, preview, or custom environments.

Schedules in 

vercel.json
can target a private Vercel Function, an HTTP path, or a Vercel Queue topic, and schedules created at runtime target a Queue topic. Any schedule can be enabled, disabled, or run on demand without redeploying.

Define a static schedule:

      
{   "schedules": {     "cleanup": {       "schedule": "0 * * * *",       "function": "api/cleanup.ts",       "timezone": "America/New_York"     }   },   "functions": {     "api/cleanup.ts": {       "experimentalTriggers": [{ "type": "schedule/v1beta" }]     }   } }

An hourly static schedule in vercel.json, targeting a private Vercel Function

Adding a 

schedule/v1beta
trigger makes the function private. It has no public URL and only the Vercel schedule infrastructure can invoke it.

Handle the dispatch:

      
import { handleSchedule } from '@vercel/schedules'; 
export const POST = handleSchedule(async (metadata) => {  console.log(`Running ${metadata.name} at ${metadata.scheduledAt}`);  await deleteExpiredRecords(); });

Handling the schedule dispatch with handleSchedule from @vercel/schedules

Create a schedule at runtime:

      
import { Schedules } from '@vercel/schedules';
await Schedules.create({  name: 'daily-digest',  target: { topic: 'digests' },  expression: { type: 'cron', cron: '0 9 * * *' },  timezone: 'America/Los_Angeles',  payload: { reportType: 'summary' },});

Creating a schedule at runtime that dispatches to a Queue topic

Schedules is the successor to Cron Jobs. Existing Cron Jobs continue to work, and the migration guide covers moving them to Schedules. Schedules also power dynamic schedules in Eve and experimental scheduled tasks in Nitro projects.

Vercel Schedules is billed starting at $5 per 1M runs and $10 per 1M creations on Pro and Enterprise. Hobby includes 500 schedule creations and 5,000 runs per month. Read the blog post for more on how Schedules works, then get started with the Schedules documentation.

entries.content:
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash from Google is now available on AI Gateway. Generate videos from text prompts with one API key and no separate Google account.

Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates 3–15 second videos with native audio and edits 3–15 second source clips with up to six reference images. Extend videos by 3–10 seconds per call, up to 30 seconds total, or refine generated clips in follow-up calls using 

previousInteractionId
. Output supports 360p, 720p, 1080p, and 4K in 16:9 or 9:16. Use 
generateText
or 
streamText
in AI SDK to receive the generated video as a file.

Copy link to headingGenerate a video

Use 

google/gemini-omni-1.2-flash
as the model name. This example generates a three-second, 360p clip and saves it as 
video.mp4
: 
      
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';import { generateText } from 'ai';
const { files } = await generateText({  model: 'google/gemini-omni-1.2-flash',  prompt: 'A red ball rolls across a white table.',  providerOptions: {    google: {      responseModalities: ['text', 'video'],      responseFormat: [        { type: 'video', resolution: '360p', duration: '3s' },      ],    },  },});
const video = files.find(file => file.mediaType === 'video/mp4');if (!video) throw new Error('No MP4 video returned');
await writeFile('video.mp4', video.uint8Array);

Copy link to headingReceive video in a streaming response

With 

streamText
, read 
fullStream
to handle generated files as they arrive. The video is delivered as a completed file: 
      
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'google/gemini-omni-1.2-flash',  prompt: 'A red ball rolls across a white table.',  providerOptions: {    google: {      responseModalities: ['text', 'video'],      responseFormat: [        { type: 'video', resolution: '360p', duration: '3s' },      ],    },  },});
for await (const part of result.fullStream) {  if (part.type === 'file' && part.file.mediaType === 'video/mp4') {    await writeFile('video.mp4', part.file.uint8Array);  } else if (part.type === 'error') {    throw part.error;  }}

entries.title: Workflow SDK adds idempotent starts
entries.summary: The Workflow SDK's start() function can now admit a run and claim a hook in one atomic step. Duplicate workflow starts fail safely. The atomic start replaces the previous getHookByToken()-then-start() pattern, whose gap between the lookup and the start left a documented duplicate-start race.Subscribe to messages inside the runThe claimed Hook exists from the moment the run is admitted, so resumeHo
entries.content:
The Workflow SDK's 

start()
function can now admit a run and claim a hook in one atomic step. Duplicate workflow starts fail safely. The atomic start replaces the previous 
getHookByToken()
-then-
start()
pattern, whose gap between the lookup and the start left a documented duplicate-start race. 
      
import { resumeHook, start } from "workflow/api";import { HookConflictError } from "workflow/errors";import { processOrder } from "./workflows/process-order";
export async function POST(request: Request) {  const { orderId, note } = await request.json();  const token = `order:${orderId}`;
  try {    const run = await start(processOrder, [orderId, note], {      experimental_hook: { token },    });    return Response.json({ runId: run.runId, started: true });  } catch (error) {    if (!HookConflictError.is(error)) throw error;    // Route the duplicate's payload to the run that owns the token    const hook = await resumeHook(token, { note });    return Response.json({ runId: hook.runId, started: false });  }}

Starting a run idempotently and routing a duplicate's payload to the run that already owns the token

Copy link to headingSubscribe to messages inside the run

The claimed Hook exists from the moment the run is admitted, so 

resumeHook
works even before the run begins executing, and early payloads are buffered and delivered in order. Inside the workflow, 
createHook({ token })
with the same token binds to the already-claimed hook: guaranteed, registering nothing new, adding no step, and resolving 
getConflict()
to 
null
. 
      
import { createHook } from "workflow";
type OrderUpdate = { note: string };
export async function processOrder(orderId: string, note: string) {  "use workflow";
  await recordNote(orderId, note);
  // Binds to the hook claimed at start: no conflict possible, no extra step  const updates = createHook({ token: `order:${orderId}` });  for await (const update of updates) {    await recordNote(orderId, update.note);  }}

Binding to the start Hook inside the run to consume payloads in order

Copy link to headingIdempotency with no extra code

The token is the idempotency key, and it comes from your own domain: an order ID, an invoice ID, an import ID, or a request ID. The token alone guarantees idempotency. Exactly one run owns it, and a duplicate 

start()
throws 
HookConflictError
carrying the owner's 
conflictingRunId
and never becomes a run. The workflow doesn't have to open the hook at all, and if it never does, the token was only an idempotency key and the run completes normally.

Setting 

experimental_minRetention
keeps the token unavailable after the run ends, counted from 
start()
, so late duplicates are still refused.

Upgrade to 

workflow
5.4.0 and read the idempotency documentation to get started.

entries.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro and its higher-speed version, Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, are now available on AI Gateway from more Zero Data Retention (ZDR) providers. Until today, Moonshot AI was the only provider serving either model.K3.1 Pro improves on earlier Kimi models in coding, 3D modeling, and financial analysis, and can carry long agent runs from a small fix to a full project. Both models have a 1M-token c
entries.content:
Kimi K3.1 Pro and its higher-speed version, Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, are now available on AI Gateway from more Zero Data Retention (ZDR) providers. Until today, Moonshot AI was the only provider serving either model.

K3.1 Pro improves on earlier Kimi models in coding, 3D modeling, and financial analysis, and can carry long agent runs from a small fix to a full project. Both models have a 1M-token context window and accept image input, and Highspeed suits interactive work like coding agents, where response time matters.

Call either model through the AI SDK, the Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. For Highspeed, use 

moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed
in place of the model name below.

Use 

moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro',  prompt: 'Write a Python function that redacts email addresses from a log line.',  providerOptions: {    gateway: {      zeroDataRetention: true,    },  },});

Setting 

zeroDataRetention
in the gateway provider options requires ZDR for that request. To require it for every request your team sends, including requests from coding agents, turn on ZDR in the AI Gateway dashboard settings. With either one on, AI Gateway routes only to providers with a ZDR agreement. If none is available for the model, the request fails instead of going to a provider without one.

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
# Upgrade to the latest version of the Vercel CLIpnpm i -g vercel@latest
# Run coding agents setup commandvercel ai-gateway coding-agents setup

Then select 

moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro
or 
moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try Kimi K3.1 Pro in the model playground.

entries.title: Introducing Vercel Schedules
entries.summary: Cron jobs are useful for work that needs to happen regularly. You can use them to do things such as back up your database on a schedule, or keep data in sync between two systems.You define them once in code and then can update them by editing their config and redeploying. But today, agents interact with users as work evolves, and schedules need to be updated in real time.We built Vercel Schedules
entries.content:
Cron jobs are useful for work that needs to happen regularly. You can use them to do things such as back up your database on a schedule, or keep data in sync between two systems.

You define them once in code and then can update them by editing their config and redeploying. But today, agents interact with users as work evolves, and schedules need to be updated in real time.

We built Vercel Schedules to allow agents and applications to create, change, or cancel one-time and recurring schedules through code, without redeploying.

Copy link to headingWhat are Vercel Schedules?

Schedules builds on the static approach used by Vercel Cron Jobs, but are designed to let users and agents decide when work should happen while your application is still running. A schedule tells Vercel when to trigger a task and where to send it. Your application provides the code that carries out the work.

You can use schedules for both static and dynamic jobs:

  • Static schedules keep the timing in 

    vercel.json
    or Build Output API configuration and sync when you deploy. You can use them to call private functions or HTTP paths, or send messages to Queue topics.

  • Dynamic schedules let your app create and manage schedules through the JS SDK, CLI, or API as it runs. They support one-time and recurring work through Queue topics.

You can also test scheduled work on Preview deployments and in custom environments before running it in Production.

Copy link to headingHow Schedules works

Take this example: A user could ask an agent with web access, “Tomorrow morning, summarize the top five stories on Hacker News.” The traditional solution would be storing the request and its schedule time in a database, then using a cron job to check for work that is due.

With Schedules, an agent can create a schedule that records the request and when to run it, without a separate database and polling job. The example below defines an AI SDK tool that gives an agent this capability.

      
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';import { tool } from 'ai';import { z } from 'zod';import { Schedules } from '@vercel/schedules';
export function scheduleTaskTool(tenantId: string, userId: string) {  return tool({    description: 'Schedule a task to run at a future time.',    inputSchema: z.object({      task: z.string().min(1).max(1000),      at: z.string().describe('Future local time: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm'),      timezone: z.string().describe('IANA time zone, e.g. America/New_York'),    }),    execute: ({ task, at, timezone }) =>      Schedules.create({        name: `agent-task-${randomUUID()}`,        namespace: tenantId,        expression: { type: 'single', at },        timezone,        target: { topic: 'agent-work' },        payload: { userId, task },      }),  });}

An AI SDK tool that creates a one-time schedule for an agent task.

When the task is due, Vercel uses Queues to deliver the saved request to your app. Your app provides code to read that request, check the user’s current permissions, and start the agent. The agent fetches the top five Hacker News posts with a web tool, then returns a summary for your app to save for the user.

If you already build agents with fx’s JavaScript library, libfx or Pi’s agent library, you can add a similar scheduling tool. The eve agent framework uses Vercel Schedules to provide dynamic scheduling tools for production agents hosted on Vercel.

Copy link to headingRun recurring application jobs

You can schedule recurring work with Vercel Schedules. Schedules can be created dynamically via the JS SDK, API, and CLI, or set up in your project’s configuration.

For example, to create a job that cleans up expired records every day, you could define a schedule that invokes a private function in your chosen time zone:

      
{  "$schema": "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json",  "schedules": {    "cleanup": {      "schedule": "0 2 * * *",      "function": "api/cleanup",      "timezone": "America/New_York"    }  },  "functions": {    "api/cleanup.ts": {      "experimentalTriggers": [        { "type": "schedule/v1beta" }      ]    }  }}

Schedules a private cleanup function for 2 a.m. New York time each day.

Vercel calls this cleanup code directly, without exposing it at a public URL. It checks that each call comes from the scheduling service, so you don’t have to add that check yourself.

If your app already uses the Nitro 3 server framework, its experimental integration lets you run the recurring jobs in your existing 

scheduledTasks
configuration as private functions.

You can also try the agent task and cleanup locally with 

vercel dev
, then test them on a Preview branch or in a custom environment before production. Use Run Schedule in your project’s Schedules tab to try either task without waiting, and see when past runs happened.

Copy link to headingGet started

Vercel Schedules is now in Public Beta, and you can use it for the recurring tasks your application already runs. When a user or agent chooses when work should happen, your code can create and manage a schedule for that task.

To get started, check out the Vercel Schedules skill and read the documentation.
